bound_context.question: What does the 58-byte leaf routine at 0x607f450 return for an options pointer, a level, a compaction style, a base level and a flag, and what do its callers depend on?

claim_anchors: semantics.tsv (15 anchors: claim -> target instruction address and bytes)
environment_limits: Static disassembly only (objdump/readelf on the digest-verified local binary); no cargo/rustc, Ghidra or a live node; the model is a Python transcription cross-checked by decoding and executing the routine's own instruction bytes, not a build of node or rocksdb.
ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 75 per family); the full 2,400-case sweep and a 20,000-input random differential are re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: From the disassembly: rdi=options, esi=level, edx=style, ecx=base, r8b=flag; the result is a single 64-bit table entry returned in rax.
The routine reads exactly one field of the options struct: options+0x1e0, a table pointer (mov 0x1e0(%rax),%rdx at 0x607f45b).
cmp %ecx,%esi with setl %al at 0x607f457/0x607f462 records level<base as a 0/1 value.
mov %edx,%edi then test %dil,%dil / setne %dil (0x607f459, 0x607f465, 0x607f468) test only style&0xff, so style=256 passes as zero and takes the subtraction path.
cmp $0x1,%r8b at 0x607f471 compares only flag&0xff against 1, so flag=257 behaves like 1 and flag=256 like 0.
or %dil,%al / jne 0x607f477 (0x607f46c, 0x607f46f): the plain level index is used when level<base or (style&0xff)!=0.

sub %ecx,%esi (0x607f480) computes level-base in 32 bits on the subtraction path and movslq %esi,%rsi (0x607f477/0x607f482) sign-extends the index; the subtraction is only reachable when level>=base, so the index is never negative.
The only table access is mov (%rdx,%rsi,8),%rax (0x607f47a and 0x607f485); there is no length load and no comparison against a bound.

result == table[level] normally, and table[level-base] when level>=base and (style&0xff)==0 and (flag&0xff)==1; validated against a decoded execution of the routine's own committed instructions over the 2,400-case sweep and 20,000 random inputs.

All 10 call sites pass the value on rather than comparing it: 7 push it as a stack argument (all seven to 0x5da8870), 2 copy it to a register (one divides by it at 0x5e105dc), 1 stores it to a stack slot.
semantics.tsv binds each semantic claim to a specific target instruction address and its bytes; verify.py regenerates it and re-reads those bytes from the binary.

unknowns: The C-level meaning of style, base and flag at each call site; they are runtime values and are not characterized here.
The length and fill order of the table at options+0x1e0, and whether any caller passes an index past its end; the routine does not bound-check.
The adjacent MaxFileSizeForL0MetaPin window at 0x607f490..0x607f4bb is not covered here.
The body is byte-identical in 3 identical source objects; only 0x607f450 is bound.
